summary: H.R. 421, the Small Business Regulatory Flexibility Improvements Act, modifies federal rulemaking requirements and procedures under the Regulatory Flexibility Act of 1980 and the Small Business Regulatory Enforcement Fairness Act of 1996. The bill expands how federal agencies must analyze the economic impacts of proposed rules and land management plans on small entities, including nonprofits and tribal organizations. It also enhances the authority of the Small Business Administration's Chief Counsel for Advocacy, alters comment-gathering and periodic review processes, expands judicial review, and waives civil fines for first-time paperwork violations by small businesses under certain conditions.

affected_groups.effect: Receive broader economic impact protections, greater inclusion in agency rule reviews, and waivers for first-time paperwork violations under specific conditions.
Must perform more detailed initial and final regulatory flexibility analyses, account for indirect effects, and conduct periodic reviews of existing rules.
Gains expanded powers to issue compliance rules, intervene in certain agency adjudications, convene review panels, and approve business size standards.
affected_groups.group: Small Business Administration (Chief Counsel for Advocacy)

affected_groups.effect: Included under revised definitions and protections relating to small organization and entity regulations.

key_provisions: Requires federal agencies to consider both direct and reasonably foreseeable indirect economic effects on small entities when determining if a rule will have a significant impact.
Expands regulatory flexibility analysis requirements to cover certain land management plan revisions or amendments by the Departments of Agriculture and the Interior.
Removes agency authority to waive regulatory flexibility analysis requirements and directs the SBA Chief Counsel for Advocacy to issue compliance rules.
Establishes review panels convened by the Chief Counsel for Advocacy to assess potential economic impacts of major rules on small entities prior to proposal.
Mandates that each agency establish a 10-year periodic review plan for existing rules that significantly affect small entities.

Prohibits federal agencies from imposing civil fines on small businesses for first-time paperwork or information collection violations, subject to specific exceptions such as public health risks or tax laws.

summary_detail.plain_summary: H.R. 421, the Small Business Regulatory Flexibility Improvements Act, modifies federal rulemaking requirements and procedures under the Regulatory Flexibility Act of 1980 and the Small Business Regulatory Enforcement Fairness Act of 1996. The bill expands how federal agencies must analyze the economic impacts of proposed rules and land management plans on small entities, including nonprofits and tribal organizations. It also enhances the authority of the Small Business Administration's Chief Counsel for Advocacy, alters comment-gathering and periodic review processes, expands judicial review, and waives civil fines for first-time paperwork violations by small businesses under certain conditions.
summary_detail.significance: The legislation modifies federal administrative procedures by increasing the analytical and procedural burdens on agencies when writing rules that affect small entities. It broadens the scope of the Regulatory Flexibility Act to include indirect economic effects, land management plans, and specific interpretive rules, while strengthening the oversight role of the Small Business Administration's Office of Advocacy.
